For years, collectors have been eagerly seeking Steve Jobs memorabilia, and a new auction item seems poised to generate significant interest. It is his eighth-grade science fair project, complete with two demonstration circuits—and a warning note Jobs gave to his teacher.

The exhibit has been stored at Jobs' family property in Los Altos ever since, but has now become one of over 200 rare items in an Apple 50th anniversary纪念 auction...

Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and RR Auctions has organized a two-part auction to mark the occasion, titled "Steve Jobs and the Computer Revolution: Apple 50th Anniversary Commemorative Auction." The first part included the very first check ever issued by the company, which sold for as much as $2.4 million.

The second part includes this science fair project.

The warning note essentially reminded the teacher that the circuits could burn out if left running for too long. As of writing, the online bidding price was still below $3,000, but it is certainly expected to change.

There is also an early Apple 1 that still works properly.

As well as a development prototype of the original iPod.
